The *Makkhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 13) is a discourse found in the *Itivuttaka* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. The text delivers a concise teaching on the abandonment of disdain or contempt (*makkha*), declaring that when the mind is cleansed of passion for contempt and abandons it, one becomes capable of bringing an end to suffering.

 Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus shows extensive formulaic reuse across the *Itivuttaka*, specifically aligning with closely structured discourses on abandoning defilements, including the *Mohapariññā Sutta* (Iti 11), *Kodhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 12), *Dosapariññā Sutta* (Iti 10), *Lobhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 9), *Mānapariññā Sutta* (Iti 8), and *Sabbapariññā Sutta* (Iti 7), as well as sharing passages with the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35) [DharmaNexus].
